src.q: Each hard capsule contains oseltamivir phosphate equivalent to 30 mg of oseltamivir.
Each hard capsule contains oseltamivir phosphate equivalent to 75 mg of oseltamivir.
Each ml of reconstituted suspension contains oseltamivir phosphate equivalent to 6 mg of oseltamivir.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Treatment of influenza in adults and children including full-term neonates with typical symptoms when influenza is circulating; efficacy shown when started within 2 days of symptom onset.

src.q: Tamiflu is indicated in adults and children including full term neonates who present with symptoms typical of influenza, when influenza virus is circulating in the community.
Efficacy has been demonstrated when treatment is initiated within two days of first onset of symptoms.

items.t: Post-exposure prevention from 1 year of age (under 1 year only during a pandemic); seasonal prevention only in exceptional situations. Not a substitute for vaccination.

src.q: Post-exposure prevention in individuals 1 year of age or older following contact with a clinically diagnosed influenza case when influenza virus is circulating in the community.
Tamiflu is not a substitute for influenza vaccination .

items.t: NICE (treatment, outside a pandemic): recommended only when national surveillance shows influenza A or B circulating, the person is in an at-risk group, and treatment can start within 48 hours of symptom onset.

src.q: Oseltamivir and zanamivir are recommended, within their marketing authorisations, for the treatment of influenza in adults and children if all the following circumstances apply
the person is in an 'at-risk' group as defined in 1.2

items.t: NICE at-risk groups: chronic respiratory, heart, renal, liver or neurological disease, diabetes, age 65 or over, or possible immunosuppression.

src.q: chronic heart disease chronic renal disease chronic liver disease chronic neurological conditions diabetes mellitus.
People who are aged 65 years or older and people who might be immunosuppressed are also defined as 'at-risk' for the purpose of this guidance.

items.t: NICE (post-exposure prophylaxis): recommended when influenza is circulating and conditions are met, including starting within 48 hours of contact and the person not effectively protected by vaccination.

src.q: Oseltamivir and zanamivir are recommended, within their marketing authorisations, for the post-exposure prophylaxis of influenza if all of the following circumstances apply.
The person has not been effectively protected by vaccination

items.t: SmPC: use only when reliable data show influenza is circulating, and take current susceptibility patterns into account.

src.q: Tamiflu should be used for the treatment and prevention of influenza only when reliable epidemiological data indicate that influenza virus is circulating in the community.

items.t: Treatment, adults and adolescents 13 years and over: 75 mg twice daily for 5 days (10 days if immunocompromised). Start as soon as possible, within 2 days of symptom onset.

src.q: The recommended oral dose is 75 mg oseltamivir twice daily for 5 days for adolescents (13 to 17 years of age) and adults.
The recommended treatment duration in immunocompromised adults and adolescents is 10 days.

items.t: Post-exposure prevention, adults and adolescents 13 years and over: 75 mg once daily for 10 days, starting within 2 days of exposure.

src.q: The recommended dose for prevention of influenza following close contact with an infected individual is 75 mg oseltamivir once daily for 10 days
Therapy should begin as soon as possible within two days of exposure to an infected individual.

items.t: Prevention during a community epidemic: 75 mg once daily for up to 6 weeks (up to 12 weeks if immunocompromised).

src.q: The recommended dose for prevention of influenza during a community outbreak is 75 mg oseltamivir once daily for up to 6 weeks

items.t: Elderly: no adjustment unless moderate or severe renal impairment.

src.q: No dose adjustment is required, unless there is evidence of moderate or severe renal impairment.

items.t: 1 to 12 years, treatment (twice daily for 5 days): 10 to 15 kg 30 mg; >15 to 23 kg 45 mg; >23 to 40 kg 60 mg; >40 kg 75 mg. Post-exposure prevention: same doses once daily for 10 days.

src.q: 10 kg to 15 kg 30 mg twice daily 30 mg twice daily > 15 kg to 23 kg 45 mg twice daily 45 mg twice daily > 23 kg to 40 kg 60 mg twice daily 60 mg twice daily > 40 kg 75 mg twice daily 75 mg twice daily
10 kg to 15 kg 30 mg once daily 30 mg once daily > 15 kg to 23 kg 45 mg once daily 45 mg once daily

items.t: Infants 0 to 12 months, treatment: 3 mg/kg twice daily for 5 days (10 days if immunocompromised). Pandemic post-exposure prevention: 3 mg/kg once daily for 10 days. Not for premature infants (<36 weeks post-conceptual age).

src.q: The recommended treatment dose for infants 0 - 12 months of age is 3 mg/kg twice daily.
This dosing recommendation is not intended for premature infants, i.e. those with a post-conceptual age less than 36 weeks.

items.t: Seasonal (epidemic) prevention not studied under 12 years. No dosing advice for children 12 years and under with renal impairment.

src.q: Prevention during an influenza epidemic has not been studied in children below 12 years of age.
There is insufficient clinical data available in infants and children (12 years of age and younger) with renal impairment to be able to make any dosing recommendation.

items.t: The oral suspension is preferred for children and adults who cannot swallow capsules or need lower doses.

src.q: Commercially manufactured Tamiflu powder for oral suspension (6 mg/ml) is the preferred product for paediatric and adult patients who have difficulties swallowing capsules or where lower doses are needed.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to oseltamivir or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Neuropsychiatric events (especially children and adolescents): monitor closely for behavioural changes and weigh continuing treatment.

src.q: Patients should be closely monitored for behavioural changes, and the benefits and risks of continuing treatment should be carefully evaluated for each patient

items.t: Effective only against influenza; protection lasts only while taking it; not a substitute for vaccination.

src.q: Oseltamivir is effective only against illness caused by influenza viruses.
The protection against influenza lasts only as long as Tamiflu is administered.

items.t: Severe renal impairment: dose adjustment needed in adults and adolescents.

src.q: Dose adjustment is recommended for both treatment and prevention in adolescents (13 to 17 years of age) and adults with severe renal impairment.

items.t: Suspension contains sorbitol (not for hereditary fructose intolerance) and sodium benzoate (may increase jaundice in newborns).

src.q: Patients with hereditary fructose intolerance (HFI) should not take thismedicinal product.
Sodium benzoate (E211) may increase jaundice in newborn babies (up to 4 weeks old).

items.t: Clinically significant interactions are unlikely (no CYP450 metabolism, low protein binding).

src.q: suggest that clinically significant drug interactions via these mechanisms are unlikely.

items.t: Take care with co-excreted medicines with a narrow therapeutic margin (e.g. methotrexate, chlorpropamide).

src.q: care should be taken when prescribing oseltamivir in subjects when taking co-excreted agents with a narrow therapeutic margin (e.g. chlorpropamide, methotrexate, phenylbutazone).

items.t: No pharmacokinetic interaction with paracetamol, aspirin, antacids, amoxicillin or warfarin (stable patients without influenza).

src.q: No pharmacokinetic interactions between oseltamivir or its major metabolite have been observed when co-administering oseltamivir with paracetamol, acetylsalicylic acid,
rimantadine or warfarin (in subjects stable on warfarin and without influenza).

items.t: Treatment (adults and adolescents 13+): CrCl >60 mL/min 75 mg twice daily; >30 to 60 mL/min 30 mg twice daily; >10 to 30 mL/min 30 mg once daily; ≤10 mL/min not recommended; haemodialysis 30 mg after each session; peritoneal dialysis 30 mg single dose.

Haemodialysis patients 30 mg after each haemodialysis session

items.t: Prevention: CrCl >60 mL/min 75 mg once daily; >30 to 60 mL/min 30 mg once daily; >10 to 30 mL/min 30 mg every second day; ≤10 mL/min not recommended; haemodialysis 30 mg after every second session; peritoneal dialysis 30 mg once weekly.

src.q: > 30 to 60 (ml/min) 30 mg (suspension or capsules) once daily > 10 to 30 (ml/min) 30 mg (suspension or capsules) every second day
Haemodialysis patients 30 mg after every second haemodialysis session

items.t: Children 12 years and under with renal impairment: insufficient data for a dose recommendation.

src.q: There is insufficient clinical data available in infants and children (12 years of age and younger) with renal impairment to be able to make any dosing recommendation.

items.t: No dose adjustment for treatment or prevention. Not studied in children with liver disease.

src.q: No dose adjustment is required either for treatment or for prevention in patients with hepatic dysfunction.

items.t: SmPC: large data (over 1000 first-trimester outcomes) show no malformative or fetal/neonatal toxicity, although one study was not conclusive for major congenital heart defects; may be considered if necessary after weighing safety, benefit and virus pathogenicity.

src.q: indicate no malformative nor feto/neonatal toxicity by oseltamivir.
the results for major congenital heart defects diagnosed within 12 months of birth were not conclusive.
The use of Tamiflu may be considered during pregnancy if necessary and after considering the available safety and benefit information

items.t: SmPC: low levels in milk (subtherapeutic for the infant); may be considered where there are clear benefits.

src.q: administration of oseltamivir may be considered, where there are clear potential benefits to breastfeeding mothers.

items.t: SPS: preferred antiviral in breastfeeding; monitor the infant for vomiting, diarrhoea, irritability and changes in sleep.

src.q: Oseltamivir is the preferred choice during breastfeeding. Infant monitoring is still required.
As a precaution, infants should be monitored for vomiting, diarrhoea, irritability, and changes in sleep.

items.t: No evidence of an effect on male or female fertility (preclinical data).

src.q: Based on preclinical data, there is no evidence that Tamiflu has an effect on male or female fertility

items.t: Adults: nausea and vomiting most common (usually on day 1 or 2, settle within 1 to 2 days); also headache. Children: vomiting most common.

src.q: the most commonly reported adverse reactions (ARs) were nausea and vomiting in the treatment studies, and nausea in the prevention studies.
In children, the most commonly reported adverse reaction was vomiting.

items.t: Rare: anaphylaxis, fulminant hepatitis/hepatic failure, angioedema, SJS/TEN, GI bleeding and neuropsychiatric events (convulsions, delirium, self-injury).

src.q: Anaphylactic and anaphylactoid reactions, hepatic disorders (fulminant hepatitis, hepatic function disorder and jaundice), angioneurotic oedema, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, gastrointestinal bleeding and neuropsychiatric disorders.

items.t: Watch closely for behavioural changes, especially in children and adolescents.

src.q: Patients should be closely monitored for behavioural changes

items.t: Check renal function (CrCl) to set the dose in adults and adolescents.

src.q: Dose adjustment is recommended for adults and adolescents (13 to 17 years of age) with moderate or severe renal impairment.

items.t: Oral. Capsules and suspension are bioequivalent; patients who cannot swallow capsules can take the suspension. The suspension is best made up by a pharmacist; oral dispensers (3 mL and 10 mL) are supplied.

src.q: Tamiflu hard capsules and Tamiflu suspension are bioequivalent formulations.
It is recommended that Tamiflu powder for oral suspension be constituted by a pharmacist prior to dispensing to the patient

items.t: Start as soon as possible (within 2 days of symptoms or exposure). It does not replace the flu vaccine.

src.q: Treatment should be initiated as soon as possible within the first two days of onset of symptoms of influenza.
Use of Tamiflu must not affect the evaluation of individuals for annual influenza vaccination.

items.t: Report unusual behaviour, confusion or hallucinations promptly, especially in children.

src.q: Neuropsychiatric events have been reported during administration of Tamiflu in patients with influenza, especially in children and adolescents.
